description: Generates a NEW segment that continues an existing video from its final frame, and returns the new job's id immediately. The result is the original clip with the new segment joined onto the end. WHEN: the user asks to extend, continue or lengthen a video, or wants to see what happens next in a clip they already have. Call `list_models` first if you have not this session: `model` and the allowed `aspect_ratio`, `resolution` and `duration` values come from there, and this tool accepts only models that can start from an image. `duration` is the length of the NEW segment, not of the finished video. Say in your `prompt` what should happen NEXT. A prompt describing the clip that already exists produces a repeat of it. THE CARD: this call has ALREADY put the aicut card in front of the user, and it fills in the finished media on its own. Do NOT call `show_generation` for this job - that adds a duplicate card; it is only for bringing back an EARLIER generation. HOW TO WAIT: call `wait_for_generation` with this job's id and `media` - it waits server-side and opens no card. While it answers `terminal: false`, wait `poll_after_seconds` and call it again; when `terminal: true`, tell the user in ONE short line what came out. Do not poll `get_video` / `get_image` / `get_audio` instead or spawn timers, and do NOT tell the user the generation is running in between. IF YOU CANNOT RENDER AN AICUT CARD (a terminal or plain SDK client), give the user the `url` from the wait result - aicut cannot see which clients render cards. TIMING: a video usually finishes in 1-3 minutes, and can take up to about 6. Do not assume it failed before then, and do not spawn timers or background shells to wait: call `wait_for_generation` (it waits server-side for up to 15 seconds per call), wait its `poll_after_seconds` and call it again, and stop when it answers `terminal: true`. `get_video` is a single immediate read for one job's raw fields - it is not the waiting loop and must not be polled in one. COST: this spends the user's tokens, priced exactly like a normal generation of the new segment - so it is the model, the duration and the resolution that decide it, not the length of the source clip. Pass `estimate_only: true` first to get the exact price. An EXTERNAL url is downloaded and stored on the account before it can be measured, which uses one of the account's daily media-ingest slots. Quoting and then creating from the SAME url costs that once, not twice - aicut reuses what it already imported - and a url already on the account costs nothing at all. SPENDS TOKENS: quote it first (`estimate_only: true`), state the price IN THE SAME MESSAGE as your ask, and wait for a go that names THIS purchase - a bare 'yes' counts only as the direct answer to that priced ask, and an ambiguous one means ask again. The full SPENDING RULES in this server's instructions apply here. IF THE USER REPORTS A CHARGE OR STEP THEY DID NOT EXPECT: re-read your own tool calls and say which you made; aicut cards cannot spend (full rule in this server's instructions). IDEMPOTENCY: `idempotency_key` is optional. Reusing a key REPLAYS the job it first created (even with different settings), so never reuse one to make another generation; the full rules are in this server's instructions (IDEMPOTENCY). OUTPUT: JSON for you to read. Tell the user the media URL plus a one-line summary; do not paste raw JSON, job ids or internal field names.

aspect_ratio.description: Output aspect ratio, one of the model's published `aspect_ratios`. REQUIRED here: the server does not guess it from the source clip, and it changes the price on some models. Match the source clip's shape unless the user asked for something else.

audio.description: Generate audio alongside the new segment, on the models that support it - `list_models` publishes this parameter for exactly those, and its description there says whether sound costs extra on that model (free on the seedance 2.x family, dearer on kling). IT DEFAULTS TO FALSE, so the new segment is SILENT unless you set it. Never set this to save the user tokens or to make a generation cheaper - set it only when the user explicitly asked for this value, and never carry it over from an earlier request.

duration.description: Length of the NEW segment in seconds, one of the model's published durations. Longer costs more. Never set this to save the user tokens or to make a generation cheaper - set it only when the user explicitly asked for this value, and never carry it over from an earlier request.

estimate_only.description: Price these exact settings and create nothing. Returns the token cost, the account balance, and whether the balance covers it. Costs nothing and changes nothing.

idempotency_key.description: Optional retry-safety key. Read the IDEMPOTENCY note in this tool's description before using one - a reused key returns the first job instead of making a new one.

model.description: Model id, exactly as `list_models` returns it. Models differ in price by more than any other setting, so use the one the user asked for and never substitute a cheaper model to save them tokens.

prompt.description: What should happen in the NEW segment.

resolution.description: Output resolution, one of the model's published options. Higher resolutions cost more. Never set this to save the user tokens or to make a generation cheaper - set it only when the user explicitly asked for this value, and never carry it over from an earlier request.

source_video.description: URL of the video to continue. Either a URL an earlier generation or upload on THIS account returned, or a genuinely external public https URL - aicut downloads it, size-caps it and stores it on the account first. An aicut-hosted URL belonging to a DIFFERENT account is refused.

name: extend_video
title: Continue a video past its ending
